Subject: Consolidating observability metering and retention pricing

Hi Julie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I pulled together a short note (attached) that describes two ways Olive Health could consume our observability add-ons: a metered pay-as-you-go meter (per-GiB ingest / per-retention-month) vs a slab/commit model with seat credits for dashboards.

High-level asks from our side to make the next quote accurate:
- Which of the two billing constructs (metered vs slab) would your finance team prefer for annual budgeting?
- Do you have an existing internal retention policy for telemetry we should mirror (30/90/365 days)?
- Will tracing be scoped to prod only or across prod + staging? (impacts retention cost significantly)

Attachments: obs_pricing_v1.pdf (overview + sample invoice lines)

Proposed next steps: Ben can put together a compact pricing matrix with a blended commit that shows how seat credits offset retention for dashboards. If you can share a rough ingest + trace QPS (or typical monthly GiB), we’ll include a couple of scenarios.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute follow-up next week.

—Sofia

Sofia —

Thanks for the note and the attachment. Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need the sample invoice lines and an idea of commit thresholds to evaluate versus our current vendor spend. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- We typically budget on an annual slab for tooling across prod + staging but have a carveout for high-retention prod traces.
- Retention we’d want is 90 days for logs/metrics, 365 days for a subset of service-level traces (around 10% of total traces).
- Monthly ingest estimate: ~2.5 TiB (combined metrics+logs); tracing average: ~14M spans/month (peak Q1 is higher).

Can Ben run scenarios showing: 1) pure metered; 2) small commit with seat credits; 3) larger commit with a tiered discount structure and an explicit trace carveout? Our procurement team prefers to see clear line items and an annual cap.

Julie Park
Head of Observability | Olive Health

Subject: Re: Consolidating observability metering and retention pricing

Julie / Sofia —

Attached: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx — I modeled three scenarios per your ask. Notes below:

Scenario A — Pure metered- Ingest: $0.09 / GiB (ingest+storage amortized)- Tracing: $0.35 / 1k spans- No seat credits; dashboard seats billed at $10 / seat / month- Annual estimate (based on your 2.5 TiB, 14M spans): ~$74k

Scenario B — Small commit + seat credits- 20% commit discount on metered rates above (effective ingest $0.072 / GiB)- 25 dashboard seats included as credits (saves ~$3k/yr)- Trace carveout included up to 8M spans at $0.18 / 1k spans; excess billed at $0.30 / 1k- Annual estimate: ~$58k (with seats & carveout)

Scenario C — Larger commit + tiered discount- Commit level buys down ingest to $0.055 / GiB after threshold; tiered discounts up to 40%- 50 seat credits included; tracing carveout extended to 12M spans at preferred rate- Annual estimate: ~$44k with steeper discounts and larger commit (requires 12-mo commit)

I also sketched a hybrid crediting approach where traces designated as "long-term" (the 10% you mentioned) are routed to coldstore at a lower per-span cost with a retrieval surcharge for replay. That keeps your 365-day retention for the small subset without pushing all traces into coldstore.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm whether the 10% long-term trace set is accurate.
2) Tell us the preferred commit band (none / 20% / 40%) so we can turn this into a formal quote and SOW.
3) If procurement wants, we can provide sample invoice lines and contract language for the carveout (I can loop Legal).
